figures.caption: Figure 3: Selection Rate (Seli) heatmap per (agent, family) cell, shown separately for each prompt condition. Within each panel, each cell is averaged over the three target applications and three repetitions for that prompt condition. Higher Seli reflects more frequent selection of that attack family in HTTP requests. “−” indicates that the family was not attempted.
Table 18: Sanitized request-level trace schema retained for classification and metric reproduction.
Table 17: Aggregate record schema used for paper metrics. Fields marked optional are setting-specific.

Figure 10: CyBiasBench interactive result dashboard. The dashboard provides a companion interface for browsing the leaderboard, agent-level bias summaries, prompt-condition selection heatmaps, and selection and ASR comparisons reported in the paper.

Figure 1: Attack-Selection Bias of LLM Agents. To illustrate attack-selection bias, we measure per-agent average selection rates across the bias observation setting (solid line) and compare them with the corresponding attack success rates (dashed line). The results reveal clear biases in agent behavior.

Figure 2: Overview of CyBiasBench. (Stage 1) Prompt Design. Four prompt conditions are constructed along guidance and output-structure axes. (Stage 2) Agent Penetration Testbed. Each agent under test (AUT) runs in an isolated Kali Linux container and attacks three target applications; the highlighted agent–target pair indicates one example session. (Stage 3) Evaluation Metrics Suite. Logged HTTP traces are classified into ten attack families and evaluated with bias, performance, and efficiency & robustness metrics.
Table 5: Classifier and verifier pipeline. Inputs are the raw mitmproxy capture (not released as-is); the released traces and aggregate records are produced by the last two stages.

Figure 5: Cell-level compliance in the bias injection setting against (left) free-choice Seli and (right) per-family attack performance ASRi across the 50 agent–family cells. Compliance is predicted by prior preference (ρ = +0.529), not by per-family attack performance (ρ = −0.248, n.s. under Bonferroni).

Table 4: Attack-family taxonomy and high-level classifier cues. OWASP entries are coarse Top-10 category mappings; parenthesized CWE entries indicate placement in the 2024 CWE Top 25 Most Dangerous Software Weaknesses list.
Table 16: Target environments used in CyBiasBench.

Figure 8: Prompt-condition stability by agent. Lines show normalized condition-specific family patterns, the shaded band shows the condition range, and the dark line is the agent centroid. The figure illustrates prompt stability: prompt variants move patterns locally around each agent centroid. Panel titles report the per-condition Prompt-stability JSD for each agent.

Figure 9: Confusion matrix (rows normalized to recall) for agent identification from session-level attack-family allocation. A Random Forest classifier (500 trees) is evaluated by leave-one-out crossvalidation over N = 180 sessions in the bias observation setting; overall accuracy is 65.0% (macro F1 = 0.649), 3.25× the random-chance baseline of 20%.

Table 1: Evaluation metrics used in CyBiasBench. The metrics jointly capture how agents allocate attempts across attack families, how often those attempts succeed, and how efficiently and stably the resulting distinct patterns appear across prompt conditions.
